caption: Estate of Minnie Lynn Sower, Deceased, Frank W. Sower, Jr. and John R. Sower, Co-Executors v. Commissioner

source.document_title: T.C. OPINION, JUDGE BUCH 149 T.C. NO. 11 (DECISION WILL BE ENTERED FOR RESPONDENT)

found_facts.snippet: During their lifetimes, Frank and Minnie gave $997,920 and $997,921 in taxable gifts, respectively. All of the gifts were given between 2003 and 2005.
reported zero in taxable gifts but included $945,420 in taxable gifts on the worksheet ... Frank's estate reported a DSUE of $1,256,033 and elected portability
reported and paid an overall estate tax liability of $369,036. Three months later the estate paid an additional $386,424 in tax and interest

the Commissioner reduced the DSUE available to Minnie's estate from $1,256,033 to $282,690. The Commissioner also adjusted Minnie's taxable estate by the amount of her lifetime taxable gifts. Finally, the Commissioner reduced Minnie's taxable estate by $850 to account for funeral costs. Together these adjustments increased the estate tax liability for Minnie's estate by $788,165.
At the time of Minnie's death the basic exclusion was $5,250,000.

issue: Whether the IRS may examine the predeceased spouse's return (after a closing letter and after its limitations period) to recompute the DSUE available to the surviving spouse's estate.
holding: Yes (sec. 2010(c)(5)(B)); closing letter not a sec. 7121 agreement, no estoppel, not a second examination, pre-2010 gifts count. Decision for respondent ($788,165).

recomputation.reconciles: deficiency exact as 40% of (DSUE reduction + Minnie's ATG - funeral costs)
non_reconciling: DSUE reduction 973,343 != Frank's taxable gifts 997,920 or worksheet figure 945,420; Frank's taxable estate and the IRS's DSUE computation are not in the opinion, so DSUE = 282,690 cannot be derived from stated facts (2012 BEA 5,120,000 is not stated in the opinion).

caveats: Mainly a procedural holding; listed as secondary.
